evidence.title: Array - JavaScript | MDN
evidence.text:
### Array indices

`Array` objects cannot use arbitrary strings as element indexes (as in an associative array")) but must use nonnegative integers (or their respective string form). Setting or accessing via non-integers will not set or retrieve an element from the array list itself, but will set or access a variable associated with that array's object property collection. The array's object properties and list of array elements are separate, and the array's traversal and mutation operations cannot be applied to these named properties.

evidence.title: Array - JavaScript | MDN
evidence.text:
JavaScript arrays are resizable and can contain a mix of different data types. (When those characteristics are undesirable, use typed arrays instead.)
 JavaScript arrays are not associative arrays and so, array elements cannot be accessed using arbitrary strings as indexes, but must be accessed using nonnegative integers (or their respective string form) as indexes.
 JavaScript arrays are zero-indexed"): the first element of an array is at index `0`, the second is at index `1`, and so on — and the last element is at the value of the array's `length` property minus `1`.
 JavaScript array-copy operations create shallow copies. (All standard built-in copy operations with any JavaScript objects create shallow copies, rather than deep copies).

claim.statement: `fs.rm` in Node.js supports a `recursive` option for deleting directories.
claim.source_sentence: In Node.js, `fs.rm` supports a `recursive` option for deleting directories.
claim.subject: Node.js

results.reason: Judges disagreed (qwen2.5:3b: supported, qwen2.5:7b: contradicted); the adjudicator decided contradicted. The claim states that `fs.rm` supports a `recursive` option for deleting directories, but all excerpts show that this option was deprecated and eventually removed starting from Node.js v16.0.0 onwards. The latest version mentioned is v25.0.0 where the option was explicitly removed.

judges.quote: The `recursive` option is deprecated, using it triggers a deprecation warning.
judges.reasoning: The excerpts indicate that the `recursive` option for `fs.rm` was deprecated in Node.js versions v14.14.0 onwards and eventually removed in version v25.0.0. This matches the claim about the `recursive` option being supported but then removed.
Excerpts from Node.js documentation show that the `recursive` option for `fs.rm` was deprecated in v16.0.0 and removed in v25.0.0, which contradicts the claim.

adjudicator.reasoning: The claim states that `fs.rm` supports a `recursive` option for deleting directories, but all excerpts show that this option was deprecated and eventually removed starting from Node.js v16.0.0 onwards. The latest version mentioned is v25.0.0 where the option was explicitly removed.

evidence.title: File system | Node.js v26.10.0 Documentation
evidence.text:
| Version | Changes |
 --- |
| v25.0.0 | Remove `recursive` option. |
| v18.0.0 | Passing an invalid callback to the `callback` argument now throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` instead of `ERR_INVALID_CALLBACK`. |
| v16.0.0 | Using `fs.rmdir(path, { recursive: true })` on a `path` that is a file is no longer permitted and results in an `ENOENT` error on Windows and an `ENOTDIR` error on POSIX. |
| v16.0.0 | Using `fs.rmdir(path, { recursive: true })` on a `path` that does not exist is no longer permitted and results in a `ENOENT` error. |
| v16.0.0 | The `recursive` option is deprecated, using it triggers a deprecation warning. |
| v14.14.0 | The `recursive` option is deprecated, use `fs.rm` instead. |

evidence.title: Deprecated APIs | Node.js v26.10.0 Documentation
evidence.text: Use `fs.rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })`, `fs.rmSync(path, { recursive: true, force: true })` or `fs.promises.rm(path, { recursive: true, force: true })` instead.
